_comment: THE ITEM EXPRESSIBILITY RATCHET. One row per case in the item gap set (tools/item-gap-vocabulary.py). `call` is the make_item arguments that SHOULD grant the wish — written for every case INCLUDING the ones that cannot work yet, which is what makes this a pre-registration rather than a description of whatever got built. `expressible` is the CURRENT truth and ItemExpressibilityTest asserts it in BOTH directions: a false row that starts rendering fails just as loudly as a true row that stops. Lighting up a capability therefore means flipping a flag in the same commit as the code, and an ACCIDENTAL unlock cannot pass unnoticed. `blocks` names what stands in the way, in the vocabulary's own terms, so the row says what to build rather than only that something is missing. See docs/ITEM_CAPABILITY_ROLLOUT.md.
_coached: `coached: true` means this wish is QUOTED VERBATIM in the make_item tool description the agent reads. That is allowed here and only here: this corpus is a tier-1 vocabulary check with no agent in it, so a quotation cannot move its number. What the mark buys is the promotion hazard — the moment such a wish is used as a ROUTING fixture or an expect_args probe it becomes a recall test, and LessonsDoNotCoachTheFixturesTest refuses that pairing. The flag is asserted in both directions, so a description that stops quoting a row must drop the mark, which is how the burn ratchets down instead of sitting here forever.
